claims: Retirement can begin as early as 62 for reduced social security benefits.
For those born in 1960 or later, full retirement age is 67.
Full Retirement Age for Social Security is 65–66 for those born 1954 or earlier.
Full Retirement Age for Social Security is 66 and 2–10 months for those born 1955–1959.
Full Retirement Age for Social Security is 67 for those born 1960 or later.
Social Security benefits can start at 62 but are permanently reduced.
Delayed retirement increases benefits by ~8% annually up to age 70.
Social Security replaces approximately 40% of the average wage earner's income.
People can work and receive benefits while retired.
Benefits may be temporarily reduced if under full retirement age and earn over a certain limit.
